sentence: A high white blood cell count is a non-specific sign, most often from infection, and doctors read it with the type of cell raised.

sentence: A full blood count measures the number and type of cells in the blood, including red cells, white cells and platelets.
note: NHS inform | edited after second pass

sentence: The test gives a total white cell count and a differential that splits white cells into types.
Those types include neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils and basophils.
Neutrophils are the main defence against bacterial infection.
A raised count is a non-specific signal, which means it does not point to one cause.
A high count can indicate infection, inflammation, or leukaemia and other blood disorders.
Infection, most often bacterial infection, is the most common cause.
Results vary with age and time of day, and older people sometimes do not show a raised count even when they have an infection.
Inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis can raise the count, and so can allergies.
Some medicines, for example corticosteroids, can raise it.
Physical or emotional stress can affect the white cell count.
Smoking and pregnancy can also raise the count.
Corticosteroids raise the white cell count partly by increasing the release of neutrophils from the bone marrow.

sentence: Physical stress can make the white cell count rise within hours, because the body holds a large store of neutrophils in the bone marrow and blood vessels.
note: added after second pass: count can double within hours after certain stimuli because of bone marrow storage and marginated pools of neutrophils

sentence: A high neutrophil count usually suggests bacterial infection, inflammation or physical stress on the body.
A high lymphocyte count can occur with viral infections or with conditions such as chronic lymphocytic leukaemia.
Leukaemia and Hodgkin disease are among the conditions that can cause a high white cell count.
note: blended summary | edited after second pass

sentence: Reactive lymphocytes on a blood film point to infection, typically viral, as the likely cause of a raised lymphocyte count.
note: added after second pass: Reactive lymphocytes seen on a blood film indicates that the most likely cause is infection, typically viral

sentence: Smoking commonly causes a mild rise in neutrophils, lymphocytes or both.
note: added after second pass: Smoking commonly causes a mild neutrophilia and/or lymphocytosis

sentence: A hospital guideline from Hampshire says a mild, lasting rise is likely to come from a chronic inflammatory or infective process, or from smoking.
The same guideline says an unexplained, very high count prompts an urgent referral to haematology.
Doctors read the count with symptoms, the differential and sometimes a repeat test or a blood film.
Reference ranges differ with age, sex and laboratory, so the report shows the range used.
The NHS says severe breathing difficulty, or someone who has passed out and is not responding normally, needs a 999 call.

sentence: For chronic myeloid leukaemia the NHS advises a non-urgent GP visit if symptoms appear.
For suspected leukaemia the NHS says a GP asks about symptoms and medical history, examines the person and sends a blood sample for testing.

sentence: A high white cell count can be caused by infection, inflammation, some medicines, stress or smoking, and less often by a blood disorder.
The differential count shows which type of white cell is raised, which helps narrow down the cause.
A mild, lasting rise is often linked to chronic inflammation, infection or smoking, while an unexplained very high count leads to urgent referral to haematology.
A single high count does not diagnose anything, and doctors may repeat the test.
